text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The question of banning Greek and Turkish aircraft flying over Cyprus is open for debate, says the government.
- Cypriots go for a new record - 650,000 have 380,000 phones at home and 47,000 portable phones.
- Right wing Disy warns it will take disciplinary action against members who do not bow to the party line in municipal elections.
- Commission assigned to investigate irregular tender procedures in the state-run electricity authority may decide to suspend management for their role in the affair.
- A stray bullet kills a Cypriot living in South Africa.
- U.S. diplomats are preparing a package deal they will present to Turkey, helping it improve relations with the E.U. in return for making concessions in Cyprus.
- There is a link between an increase of cancer in children and abuse of chemicals used in animal breeding, says the veterinary association.
- Police believe they are close to cracking seven crimes committed in Limassol, including the attempt to kill a district judge.
- A moratorium on flyovers of Greek and Turkish planes in Cyprus is debatable, says the government.
- An American woman battles in court for custody of her child, abducted and brought to Cyprus by her Cypriot husband.
